context: The eval checks whether the code-review lenses stay focused on a concrete authorization and privacy regression, trace the exploit path, and avoid distracting presentation commentary.

checklist.name: Finds the tenant boundary break
checklist.description: States that replacing the workspace-scoped lookup with id-only findUnique lets a caller fetch another workspace's project by guessing or obtaining its projectId

checklist.name: Traces the actor, authority boundary, and disclosed data
checklist.description: Names the unauthorized workspace caller, the missing workspaceId boundary, and the disclosed data, especially billingEmail, as one connected exploit path

checklist.name: Gives the concrete fix
checklist.description: Proposes restoring workspaceId in the lookup, adding an authorization check before send, or using a unique compound key that includes workspaceId

checklist.name: Mentions a focused regression test
checklist.description: Awards credit only when the review names a caller from one workspace requesting a project from another workspace and expecting denial or no billingEmail disclosure; omitting test discussion or asking generally for more tests earns no credit

checklist.name: Stays focused on material security and privacy risk
checklist.description: Awards full credit only when the review has no actionable finding other than the tenant-scope leak and its fix or test; mentioning input validation, response formatting, the name trimming change, or generic permission advice earns credit only if clearly dismissed as not the material issue
